title: GS21 gvy25s at gamma_v 0.5, bv_comp 9.0: the mirrored ladder's level shifts kept, the y price cut
question: Does GS21 produce KP14's hump when the market channel that the level compensation opens is as large as the y channel?
notes:
DIAGNOSIS (2026-10-29, bop_runs/probe/hump_decomp.py). Type EW portfolio returns regressed on the EW market and dy: in vyg25s market beta rises with b, concavely (0.71, 0.87, 1.00, 1.10, 1.19, 1.27) while the residual premium falls (+0.02, +0.10, +0.10, +0.03, -0.07, -0.23 %/mo): two priced channels opposed, with different curvature, sum to the hump. In bvychs both rise with b (beta 0.89 -> 1.19, residual -0.33 -> +0.44). In gvy25s they oppose (market part 0.36 -> 0.26) but the y channel (-0.59 -> +0.71) is ten times the market one, so the sum is monotone.

DESIGN. gs_ashift = -bv_comp log W(b), and log W is about proportional to gamma_v, so gamma_v 0.5 with bv_comp 9.0 keeps (sq) or raises (sh) gvy25s's level shifts (+-0.6; sh +-1.0) while the y premium falls to 20% of gvy25s's. The shifts move profitability, and with it the market beta, in the direction opposite to y.

PREDICTION (2026-10-29): the type premium turns non-monotone (peak inside the ladder) in at least half the seeds; room rises above gvy25s's 11%, gap +0.00 to +0.02. SR_max falls toward gsbase's 0.29 because y is cheaper. Falsified if the premium stays monotone in b.
